content.title: 9 Remote Work Tips Nobody Tells You
content.text:
Remote work has gone from a perk to the default for many engineering teams, but most advice about it is the same recycled list of get dressed and take breaks. We wanted to go a bit deeper. Here are 9 remote work tips nobody tells you, gathered from years of working with distributed teams. Some of them might surprise you.

1. Over-communicate on purpose — In an office people can see you are busy. At home, nobody can. Post a short update when you start a task and when you finish it. It feels excessive at first, but your teammates will thank you.

2. Create a shutdown ritual — Without a commute, the workday has no natural end. Pick a small ritual, like closing your laptop and putting it in a drawer, to signal that you are done. Your evenings will get their boundaries back.

3. Invest in your chair before your monitor — Everyone talks about screens, but the chair is what you sit in for eight hours. A good chair prevents the back pain that sneaks up after a few months of remote work.

4. Keep your camera on sometimes — You do not need it on for every meeting, but turning it on for the important ones builds trust. People remember faces more than voices.

5. Write things down — Decisions made in a video call vanish the moment the call ends. Follow up with a short written summary so everyone, including people in other time zones, knows what was agreed.

6. Schedule social time — Nobody bumps into you at the coffee machine anymore. Set up a casual weekly call with no agenda. It feels awkward the first time and valuable every time after.

7. Move your body every hour — Set a reminder to stand up, stretch, or walk around the room. Sitting still for hours is worse at home because there is nowhere to walk to.

8. Separate your work devices — If you can, keep work on one machine and personal life on another. When the work laptop is closed, work is closed. It makes disconnecting far easier.

9. Learn your team's time zones — Know when your colleagues are online and plan around it. A message sent at the right time gets an answer in minutes; the same message at the wrong time waits until tomorrow.

So there you have it: 9 remote work tips nobody tells you. Remote work is a skill like any other, and small adjustments to your habits compound into a much better experience over time. Try a couple of these this week and see which ones stick. What is the remote work tip that changed things for you? Let us know in the comments and share this post with a colleague who is still figuring it out.
